title: Hammurabi becomes king of Babylon
text: Hammurabi succeeds his father Sin-muballit and proclaims a debt remission (mīšarum). Shamshi-Adad dominates the north, Rim-Sin of Larsa the south (he had taken Isin two years earlier).

title: Raid on Uruk and Isin
text: Hammurabi's year-7 name celebrates seizing Uruk and Isin from Larsa, but both soon return to Rim-Sin.

title: Malgium pays tribute
text: Allied with Shamshi-Adad and Eshnunna, Hammurabi defeats Malgium, which buys peace with 15 talents of silver (year 10 name).

title: Rapiqum added to Babylon
text: Shamshi-Adad takes Rapiqum on the Euphrates from Eshnunna and hands it to Hammurabi (year 11 name).

title: Shamshi-Adad's Zagros campaign
text: Shamshi-Adad and Ishme-Dagan campaign against Qabra and Arbela; letters to Kuwari of Shusharra document the war.

title: Death of Shamshi-Adad
text: The founder of the Kingdom of Upper Mesopotamia dies (c. 1776/1775). His realm fragments; Ishme-Dagan keeps Ekallatum and Assur.

title: Zimri-Lim takes Mari
text: With Yamhad's backing Zimri-Lim ousts Yasmah-Addu and becomes king of Mari, marrying Shibtu, daughter of Yarim-Lim of Aleppo.

title: 'No king is strong by himself'
text: A Mari letter of this period: 'Ten or fifteen kings follow Hammurabi of Babylon, as many follow Rim-Sin of Larsa, Ibal-pi-El of Eshnunna and Amut-pi-El of Qatna; twenty kings follow Yarim-Lim of Yamhad.' (approximate date)

title: Elam invades and takes Eshnunna
text: The sukkalmah Siwe-palar-huppak, with Babylon and Mari initially as allies, captures Eshnunna and pushes up the Tigris (approx. 1766-1765).

title: Elam turns on Babylon
text: Elamite armies besiege Razama and occupy Shubat-Enlil; Elam demands Babylon's submission. Hammurabi and Zimri-Lim form a coalition; Rim-Sin stays aloof.

title: Elamite coalition defeated
text: Hammurabi's year-30 name records defeating the army of Elam with Subartu, Gutium, Eshnunna and Malgium. Elam withdraws.

title: Fall of Larsa
text: After Mashkan-shapir surrenders and a siege of about six months, Larsa falls; Rim-Sin is captured. Hammurabi rules all of Sumer and Akkad (year 31 name).

title: Eshnunna defeated
text: Babylon defeats the armies of Eshnunna, Subartu and Gutium (year 32 name) and takes Mankisum on the Tigris.

title: Mari conquered
text: Hammurabi turns on his ally Zimri-Lim and takes Mari (year 33 name). The same year he digs the canal 'Hammurabi is the abundance of the people' supplying Nippur, Eridu, Ur, Larsa, Uruk and Isin.

title: Mari and Malgium destroyed
text: Hammurabi demolishes the walls of Mari and Malgium (year 35 name). Mari's palace is burnt - preserving the 20,000-tablet archive found in the 1930s.

title: Ziggurat of Kish rebuilt
text: Year 36: Hammurabi restores the temple-tower of Zababa and Inanna at Kish.

title: Northern campaign
text: Hammurabi defeats Subartu, Turukkum and Gutium (year 37 name); he campaigns again in the north in later years.

title: Eshnunna flooded
text: Year 38: Hammurabi destroys Eshnunna 'with a great flood' - perhaps by breaching Diyala dykes.

title: Code of Hammurabi
text: Approximate date of the Code: 282 laws under a relief of Hammurabi before Shamash, set up in temples (one copy probably at Sippar). The basalt stele was carried to Susa c. 1158 BC and found there in 1901.

title: Death of Hammurabi
text: Hammurabi dies in his 43rd year; his son Samsu-iluna inherits an empire that will begin to break apart within a decade (revolt of Rim-Sin II, 1739).
